title: Credits Set Off When Rider Premium Arrears are Settled
content:
The credits standing on the premium account of one of the Optional Supplemental Benefit Riders are set off against the money the member is asked for according to the rider's standing.

## The rule

1. Where the rider stands ended, nothing is set off, a credit standing on an ended rider being paid back to the member.
2. Where the rider stands suspended for unpaid premium, every credit posted to the rider premium account is set off.
3. Otherwise, the credits posted to the rider premium account within the days of grace the rider held allows are set off.

## Restated as condition and amount

| The rider's standing | The credits set off |
|---|---|
| Ended | Nothing; such a credit is paid back to the member |
| Suspended for unpaid premium | Every credit on the account |
| Any other standing | Those posted within the days of grace the rider held allows |

## Worked on hypothetical inputs

A rider premium account carries credits of 12.40 USD and 6.00 USD, the first posted three calendar months before the month of handling and the second in the month of handling; the rider allows days of grace amounting to a span of 2 whole months.

- **Ended:** nothing is set off. The 18.40 USD standing in credit is paid back to the member rather than taken against what is owed.
- **Suspended for unpaid premium:** both are set off, 18.40 USD.
- **Any other standing:** only the 6.00 USD posted within the span is set off.

## Note

The first of the three cases turns on the rider standing ended and takes precedence over the second: a rider that has ended sets off nothing, whatever its account carries.
